blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 7 killings of trans people (trans women and people of a local trans-feminine identity category) in 2025 - the second-highest count band nationally (two states recorded 8 each). Against a population of ~9.4 million this yields roughly 0.74 per million per year, nearly double the national figure (~0.38 per million: 80 killings across ~211 million people). The state/province also hosts the country's best-known historic coastal tourist corridor, so the concentration of killings directly overlaps with visitor traffic and visible trans presence in public coastal spaces.

Identical absolute counts mask different densities: one other state recorded the same 7 killings in 2025 on a population of ~15 million - about 0.47 per million against this state/province's ~0.74 - and both share the visitor-coast overlap.

No local legal restriction or ordinance was identified. The exposure is violence-driven and location-dependent: a trans visitor staying in the capital's centre or the adjacent historic city is in the same geography where the killings cluster.
